item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00310","case1_error":"Omits the 20% primer discount, charging full price.","case2_error":"Subtracts coupon savings from the amount paid instead of adding them to recover full price; also mislabels dollars as cents.","reason":"Ignoring a discount differs from reversing its effect when reconstructing the original price.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00311","case1_error":"Multiplies area by coverage before dividing by coverage, leaving the area value incorrectly interpreted as gallons.","case2_error":"Treats two friends' combined donut allocation as each new friend's allocation, then mishandles extras and Andrew's share.","reason":"The first misuses a coverage rate; the second confuses group totals with individual allocations.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00312","case1_error":"Reduces the required rope length by 25% instead of compensating for rope lost during lashing.","case2_error":"Invents three planks per leg despite the stated requirement of one plank per leg.","reason":"Applying loss to the required length differs from replacing an explicit per-leg requirement with an invented value.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00313","case1_error":"Treats the brother's entire pre-purchase balance as Michael's transfer and answers Michael's initial money instead of the brother's.","case2_error":"Assigns the brother's lifting formula and weight to Felix, ignoring the stated relationships needed to calculate Felix's capacity.","reason":"The first reconstructs and reports the wrong person's initial money; the second explicitly calculates Felix's capacity using an erroneous relation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00314","case1_error":"Divides Grenada's supplies between bases, invents equal base totals, omits guns, and makes additional numerical errors.","case2_error":"Subtracts the overlap from both sprays' kill percentages, excluding germs killed by both from the total killed.","reason":"Inventing an allocation and equality between bases differs from double-subtracting an overlap when calculating a union.","judgment":"different"}]}
